rooms.name: Lock Approach
rooms.description: A ribbon of grass grows at each old waterline. The lowest ribbon is green on the underside.

rooms.name: Upper Apron
rooms.description: Water fans over the lip in a sheet thin enough to read the chisel marks underneath.

rooms.name: Needle Door
rooms.description: A narrow wicket can be moved by one keeper. A painted hand warns against touching the red main gate.

rooms.name: Gauge House
rooms.description: Three floats hang over a table. The float for the lower town twitches twice for each movement of the lake.

encounters.cue: Orin the gauge keeper counts the tremors on his knuckles. He would trust a float before a signed order.
encounters.result: Orin explains that DRAW and FILL at the trial weir are reversible. Only the master seat can pin the gates for good.

rooms.name: Trial Weir
rooms.description: Two small wheels marked DRAW and FILL let a keeper test the lake level before fixing the main gates. A board charts the ferry and the salt rail.

encounters.cue: Turn DRAW to lower the trial lake. The ferry will ground and the rail will emerge.
encounters.result: The water drops to trial level. Iven grounds on mud; the salt track and its trim siding emerge. FILL can reverse the trial here.
encounters.hint: DRAW requires a high lake and unpinned master gates.

encounters.cue: Turn FILL to float the ferry and submerge the track again.
encounters.result: The lake refills. The ferry floats and the salt rail disappears under brine again.
encounters.hint: FILL requires a low lake and unpinned master gates.

changes.text: The locking pin is still hanging beside the trial wheels; either trial can be undone here.
A steel pin locks DRAW in place. Water leaves by the cliff spillway; there will be no refill trial.
Both trial wheels are pinned. The gauge for the lower houses has gone dark; the lake float rides high.
Both trial wheels are pinned. The floats move a little with each stroke and settle at ferry height.

rooms.name: Keeper's Sink
rooms.description: A porcelain basin catches samples. Dry crystals in the plughole taste bitter long after the water has gone.

rooms.name: Wick Channel
rooms.description: A long felt wick lifts water over a wall and feeds a row of gardens on the other side.

rooms.name: Fish Stair
rooms.description: Minnows nose into grooves cut by a keeper too fond of fish to close the channel outright.

rooms.name: Stoplog Yard
rooms.description: Oak beams rest in numbered slots. The lowest beam was replaced by three cabin doors nailed together.

rooms.name: Silt Chapel
rooms.description: Names of lock accidents are pressed into silt bricks. Deep water has blurred the oldest letters.

rooms.name: Gate Teeth
rooms.description: A chipped pinion catches every ninth turn. The old keeper marked the bad tooth with white chalk.

rooms.name: Float Run
rooms.description: A cork float slides up a guide taut as a harp string. Its shadow points to the salt line.

rooms.name: Leech Basin
rooms.description: The clear pool was once the surgeon's supply. A small ferry token lies beyond the reach of the leeches.

rooms.name: Tow Hook
rooms.description: The towline from the ferry has peeled a single iron hook almost straight.

rooms.name: Spill Stair
rooms.description: Blue tiles are slippery under the seep. Each has a small notch at the safe edge for a keeper's boot.

rooms.name: Maintenance Sling
rooms.description: A patched sling hangs over the needle bearings. The patch carries the badge of the lantern district.

rooms.name: Salt Ladder
rooms.description: The smell of brine rises from the old railway. An access ladder reaches its dry head platform.

rooms.name: Lock Kitchen
rooms.description: A kettle hangs at each historic flood height. The top one has never been used.

rooms.name: Whitewater Lip
rooms.description: Foam swallows all sound except the bass note from the master dam.

rooms.name: Relief Flume
rooms.description: The shallow flume leads toward three springs. A diagram scratched in the slime shows water meeting itself.
